title: SNMP (Simple Network Management Protocol)
summary: SNMP is a protocol for network management. Managers query agents on devices. Operations: Get (read), GetNext (read next), GetBulk (read many), Set (write), Trap (unsolicited notification), Inform (acknowledged notification). Data is organized in a MIB (Management Information Base) tree of OIDs (Object Identifiers). SNMPv3 adds authentication and encryption.

structure.meaning: Read a value: Get(varbind list). Returns the values.
Read the next value in the MIB tree (lexicographic). Used for walking tables.
Read many values at once. More efficient than repeated GetNext.
Write a value: Set(varbind list). Returns confirmation.
Unsolicited notification from agent to manager. E.g., linkDown, coldStart, authenticationFailure.
Object Identifier: dotted decimal (e.g., 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.1.0 = sysDescr.0). Hierarchical tree.
Variable binding: OID + value (or NULL for Get). Value types: integer, string, counter, gauge, timeticks, OID, IP address, etc.
Shared secret for authentication (plaintext, sent in every packet). 'public' is the default (insecure).
User-based Security Model: username + auth protocol (MD5/SHA) + priv protocol (DES/AES). Replaces community strings.

notes: SNMPv1 (1988), v2c (1996), v3 (2002). v3 adds authentication and encryption.
MIB (Management Information Base) defines the OID tree for each device type.
SNMP is the standard for network device management (routers, switches, servers).
SNMP is being superseded by NETCONF/YANG for modern network automation.
